what_it_does: This paper designs a direct digital transmitter (a circuit that generates and broadcasts RF signals) for K/Ka-band (24 GHz) capable of transmitting at 3.2 gigabits per second with low error rate (measured by EVM, error vector magnitude). The transmitter must work efficiently at both peak power and back-off power (reduced power for efficiency during light traffic). Conventional transmitter designs combine two channels of data using a summing network that loses 3 decibels (half) of the power. The paper proposes a multiphase subharmonic switching architecture: it uses a low-frequency clock divided down from the RF frequency (subharmonic), applies phase shifts to attenuate unwanted harmonic spurs (clock noise at multiples of the frequency), and employs a hybrid DAC (digital-to-analog converter) that uses noise shaping to enable high-speed operation while maintaining clean, low-error signals.
